key_insight: A symmetric graded-mesh Galerkin FEM with L1 time discretization is developed for time-fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant delay, enabling rigorous stability and convergence analysis via an auxiliary-variable reformulation.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical and theoretically justified solver for delayed fractional dynamics in computational mechanics and diffusion-type engineering models where nonlocal time effects matter.
method: Reformulate the delayed fractional PDE into a coupled system using a symmetric fractional-order reduction and an auxiliary variable w.
Discretize in time with the L1 scheme on a symmetric graded mesh and in space with standard finite elements.
Prove stability and error bounds using a discrete fractional Grönwall inequality plus a new comparison principle and barrier function.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that confirm the derived stability and convergence results across the proposed mesh and discretization settings.
watch_item: Performance and error behavior depend on careful construction of the symmetric graded time mesh and barrier functions, so implementation details may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
